about.studioCaption: In the studio — studies of light and shadow
about.bio1: Born in Tielt, Belgium, in 1966. I now live and work in Ghent. My journey in the arts began with color pencils and grew into a lifelong exploration of visual expression. I earned a Master's degree in Art History from Ghent University, followed several years later by two years of Textile Design studies at KASK in Ghent. At the Royale Académie Internationale d’Été de Wallonie I deepened my study of the old masters — glazing and optical mixing.
about.bio2: My work is a personal and passionate quest to express and capture the fragility and the delicate essence of life. I create in dialogue with nature, drawn to the interplay between light and shadow, the infinite and the transitory, the dynamic and the static. In May 2026 I took part in a residency at Convento de Mértola (Portugal), working with Japanese paper and the rhythms of wind, light and shadow — a turning point that placed natural processes at the centre of my practice.
about.mediumPaintingDesc: Abstract and observational work inspired by nature. Oil works in progress look at light and ever-changing shadows; acrylic pieces such as Breathing in & breathing out (24 × 30 cm, 2022) explore stillness and breath on canvas.
about.mediumPhotographyDesc: I often choose watercolor and gouache for their delicate and fluid language — botanical studies, plants and florals, and pieces such as Vagues, Gigaro for World Oceans Day.
about.mediumTextileDesc: The tactility and textures of textile are increasingly woven into my artistic language — adding a physical, layered dimension to my visual explorations, including ecoprint on linen from residency research.
about.approachQuote: Work in progress — inspired by nature, observing light and ever changing shadows.
about.approach: I work intuitively, translating impressions and emotions into visual form. My process begins with a sense of calm and focus — a counterbalance to the complexity of contemporary life. Whether painting in oil, layering watercolor washes, or studying shadows on Japanese paper in the wind, a central aim is to create a quiet moment for the viewer, a space that invites personal interpretation and reflection.
